message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes of all time. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high‑school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the 2003 Mr. Basketball America and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the 2003 draft. LeBron quickly became a dominant force in the league, earning the NBA Rookie of the Year award in 2004. Over his career, he has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), the Miami Heat (2010–2014), and the Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). He has won four NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) and earned four NBA Finals MVP awards.

Beyond the court, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the I PROMISE School in Akron—a public school for at‑risk children. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment, and starring in the 2018 film “Space Jam: A New Legacy.” LeBron’s impact extends into social activism, where he has spoken out on issues such as racial equality, education reform, and voting rights.
